 'statement':'The target states two separate componentwise backward-error representations of a specified real-arithmetic computation: zero-pad the vectors, multiply entries with prescribed relative errors, accumulate each block sequentially, and accumulate the block results sequentially. The perturbation bound uses gamma(T + B - 1, u), where B is the block count. A further hypothesis uses d(B) = Nat.clog 2 B. The definition of Nat.clog is not supplied, so the exact mathematical meaning of that hypothesis cannot be fully determined from the supplied data. No tree reduction is defined by these constructions.',
 'targets':[{
  'name':'BlockDotProduct.block_dot_product_sequential',
  'statement':'For every n,T in the natural numbers with n > 0 and T > 0, every real u >= 0, every pair of functions x,y : {0,...,n-1} -> R, and every trace in RoundingTrace(u), define B = blockCount(n,T) = floor((n+T-1)/T), d(B) = Nat.clog 2 B (whose definition is absent), and m = T+B-1. Natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero; here positivity makes these displayed subtractions ordinary subtraction. Assume both (T+d(B))*u < 1 and m*u < 1, with natural numbers embedded into R in these products. There exist functions Delta_x,Delta_y : {0,...,n-1} -> R such that, writing Q = sequentialBlockDotProduct(x,y,T,trace), all four assertions hold simultaneously: Q = sum_{i=0}"'^{n-1} (x(i)+Delta_x(i))*y(i); for every i in {0,...,n-1}, |Delta_x(i)| <= gamma(m,u)*|x(i)|; Q = sum_{i=0}''^{n-1} x(i)*(y(i)+Delta_y(i)); and for every such i, |Delta_y(i)| <= gamma(m,u)*|y(i)|. Here gamma(m,u) = (m*u)/(1-m*u), whose denominator is positive under the hypothesis. Q is exactly the two-level sequential recurrence described in the constructions, with the supplied trace determining all errors. The two equalities perturb one input at a time; they do not assert an equality using both perturbations together.'"'
 }],
 'constructions':[
  {'name':'BlockDotProduct.blockCount','description':'A function of arbitrary n,T in N: blockCount(n,T) = ((n+T) dotminus 1) div T, where dotminus denotes subtraction truncated at zero and div is natural-number division. For T > 0 this is ceil(n/T), including zero when n=0. At T=0, natural-number division by zero returns zero. In the target, B = blockCount(n,T) is positive and counts the blocks processed.'},
  {'name':'BlockDotProduct.treeDepth','description':'A function N -> N defined by treeDepth(B) = Nat.clog 2 B. No definition or characterizing property of Nat.clog is included, so its precise mathematical meaning, including boundary values, is unavailable. This value enters the target hypothesis (T+treeDepth(B))*u < 1. It is not used to compute sequentialBlockDotProduct, and no tree algorithm is defined here.'},
  {'name':'BlockDotProduct.gamma','description':'For every m in N and u in R, gamma(m,u) = ((m cast to R)*u)/(1-(m cast to R)*u), using real division. This is a total formal definition with no positivity or nonzero-denominator hypothesis (real division by zero has value zero in this formal arithmetic). The target uses m = T+B-1 and assumes m*u < 1, making the denominator positive.'},
  {'name':'BlockDotProduct.zeroExtend','description':'For an implicit n in N and any x : Fin n -> R, zeroExtend(x) : N -> R sends i to x(i) when i<n, using the corresponding element of Fin n, and to zero otherwise. Fin n is the set of natural indices 0 <= i < n.'},
  {'name':'BlockDotProduct.RoundingTrace','description':'A family of data types indexed by an arbitrary real u. Its supplied single constructor RoundingTrace.mk takes functions productError,blockAddError : N -> N -> R and reductionError : N -> R, together with proofs that for every b,t in N, |productError(b,t)| <= u and |blockAddError(b,t)| <= u, and for every b in N, |reductionError(b)| <= u. These are its three error fields and three bound-proof fields. The supplied projections retrieve the three functions. This is bounded prescribed-error data, not an algorithm or a specification of a concrete rounding rule. All bounds hold at all natural indices, including unused ones. An inhabitant necessarily has u >= 0; the target also assumes this explicitly.'},
  {'name':'BlockDotProduct.sequentialSum','description':'For any entry,error : N -> R, define S(k) = sequentialSum(entry,error,k) for k in N by S(0)=0, S(1)=entry(0), and S(k+1)=(S(k)+entry(k))*(1+error(k)) for every k>=1. Thus a sum of length L processes entries 0 through L-1 in order. The first entry is copied without applying an addition error; error(0) is never used. For L>=1, only error(1),...,error(L-1) are used. The definition itself imposes no error bounds.'},
  {'name':'BlockDotProduct.roundedProduct','description':'For implicit n in N and u in R, x,y : Fin n -> R, trace : RoundingTrace(u), and arbitrary T,b,t in N, roundedProduct(x,y,trace,T,b,t) = zeroExtend(x,b*T+t)*zeroExtend(y,b*T+t)*(1+trace.productError(b,t)). All operations in this expression after indexing are real arithmetic. This applies a supplied relative perturbation to the exact product; it does not compute a machine-format rounding operation. If b*T+t>=n the result is zero.'},
  {'name':'BlockDotProduct.blockPartial','description':'For implicit n in N and u in R, x,y : Fin n -> R, T in N, trace : RoundingTrace(u), and b in N, blockPartial(x,y,T,trace,b) is sequentialSum(entry,error,T) with entry(t)=roundedProduct(x,y,trace,T,b,t) and error(t)=trace.blockAddError(b,t). It processes exactly T positions b*T through b*T+T-1, including zero-padded positions. For T=0 it is zero; for T>=1 the first rounded product is copied, then each subsequent product is added and the entire running sum is multiplied by 1+blockAddError(b,t), for t=1,...,T-1. Padded zeros still participate in these later recurrence steps.'},
  {'name':'BlockDotProduct.sequentialBlockDotProduct','description':'For implicit n in N and u in R, x,y : Fin n -> R, T in N and trace : RoundingTrace(u), let B=blockCount(n,T). The value is sequentialSum(entry,error,B), where entry(b)=blockPartial(x,y,T,trace,b) and error(b)=trace.reductionError(b). If B=0 it returns zero. If B>=1 it copies block 0, then for b=1,...,B-1 replaces the running result R by (R+blockPartial(x,y,T,trace,b))*(1+trace.reductionError(b)). It therefore combines the B block results sequentially; reductionError(0) is unused. This is the exact constructed quantity Q appearing in both equalities of the target theorem.'}
 ],
 'assumptions':[
  'Natural numbers include zero; Fin n denotes the indices i with 0 <= i < n. Vector entries, errors, recurrence values, and perturbations are real numbers. Natural-number subtraction is truncated; casts in the theorem embed natural numbers into R.',
  'The target universally quantifies n,T in N with n>0 and T>0, u in R with u>=0, x,y : Fin n -> R, and trace : RoundingTrace(u).',
  'The trace carries the bounds |productError(b,t)|<=u and |blockAddError(b,t)|<=u for all b,t in N, and |reductionError(b)|<=u for all b in N.',
  'With B=blockCount(n,T), the target additionally requires (T+treeDepth(B))*u<1 and (T+B-1)*u<1. Both are retained as distinct hypotheses.',
  'No concrete floating-point format, rounding rule, sign restrictions on x or y, independence assumptions on errors, or exact divisibility of n by T is specified.'
 ],
 'missing_context':['The definition or mathematical specification of Nat.clog is absent. It is needed to translate treeDepth(B)=Nat.clog 2 B, and hence the target hypothesis (T+treeDepth(B))*u<1, into fully specified ordinary mathematics without inferring meaning from a declaration name.']
}
assert [t['name'] for t in out['targets']]==src['targets']
assert [c['name'] for c in out['constructions']]==src['construction_names']
assert set(out)=={'schema_version','candidate_hash','status','statement','targets','constructions','assumptions','missing_context'}
fd,tmp=tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.translation-',suffix='.json',dir='/output')
try:
    with os.fdopen(fd,'w') as f:
        json.dump(out,f,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)
        f.write('\\n')
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())
    os.replace(tmp,'/output/translation.json')
finally:
    if os.path.exists(tmp): os.unlink(tmp)
print('Saved /output/translation.json; validated exact target/construction coverage and required fields; status='+out['status'])
PY"
